definitions.explanation: To look at and comprehend written text. Used for books, newspapers, signs, emails, and any written material.
To speak written words out loud, as in reading poetry or reading to someone.
To anticipate or predict something, as in 'reading' a situation or someone's intentions. {空気|くうき}を{読|よ}む means to read the atmosphere/room.

examples.japanese: {毎日|まいにち}{新聞|しんぶん}を{読|よ}みます。
examples.english: I read the newspaper every day.

examples.japanese: この{漢字|かんじ}は{読|よ}めません。
{空気|くうき}を{読|よ}んでください。

notes: {読|よ}む is a godan verb with the te-form {読|よ}んで. The expression {空気|くうき}を{読|よ}む (read the air/atmosphere) is very common in Japanese culture and refers to understanding social cues and unspoken expectations. Someone who can't do this is called KY ({空気読|くうきよ}めない).
